info.title: API.SH: JCPenney
info.description: The JCPenney API from API.SH: public JCPenney data as clean JSON. Every endpoint is a GET with query parameters and your key in the x-api-key header. Calls that run cost the credits shown (x-credits): successes, and lookups that found nothing (404). Refused calls and errors on our side are free. Docs: https://api.sh/docs · Every platform: https://api.sh/openapi.json

get.description:
jcpenney.com's category tree: departments and their categories with ids and product counts, to the depth asked. Use an id with /jcpenney/v1/search as `category`.

Every response includes `credits_used`: the credits this call cost.

Price: 1 credit per successful call. Docs: https://api.sh/docs/jcpenney-categories

parameters.name: parent
parameters.description: A department or category id (e.g. dept20000018 for shoes); empty for the top level.

200.description: The data as JSON (or CSV / NDJSON with `output`).

get.description:
One jcpenney.com product: name, brand, description, rating, review, question and answer counts, category and breadcrumbs, badges, every image, options (size, color, width…) with in-stock flags, each lot's description, bullet points, specifications, shipping notes and limits, and every variant (SKU) with its options, size, UPC, in-stock flag and stock level. `offers` has the prices for the chosen SKU or the first SKU of each lot: original, sale and clearance price with percent off, coupon codes with the price after the coupon, and ship-to-home quantity and delivery date (to `zip` when given).

Every response includes `credits_used`: the credits this call cost.

Price: 1 credit per successful call. Docs: https://api.sh/docs/jcpenney-product

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: JCPenney product id (ppr5008310825) or a jcpenney.com /p/ product link.

parameters.name: sku
parameters.description: A variant id from variants[].sku: offers then shows that SKU's prices and delivery.

parameters.name: zip
parameters.description: 5-digit US ZIP code for the delivery date.

200.description: The data as JSON (or CSV / NDJSON with `output`).

get.description:
Customer reviews of one jcpenney.com product with the average rating, review count, recommended counts, star distribution and secondary rating averages. Each review has rating, title, text, date, nickname, location, recommended flag, helpful votes, photos, badges and any brand response. Sort and filter by stars, photos or words. Pass `next_page` back as `page`; it is null on the last page.

Every response includes `credits_used`: the credits this call cost.

Price: 1 credit per successful call. Docs: https://api.sh/docs/jcpenney-reviews

get.description:
Search the jcpenney.com catalog by keywords, or browse a category or brand, with every filter and sort the site offers. Each product has id, name, brand, link, images, price and price type (sale, clearance, original), list price, coupon price and code, final price after coupon, percent off, rating and review count, badges, clearance, online-only and store-pickup flags, same-day pickup availability, in-stock flag, description, and every color variant with its own price, sizes, image and link. The response also has every filter with values and counts (`facets`), matching categories and related searches. Use `store` to list only products available for pickup at one store. Pass `next_page` back as `page`; it is null on the last page.

Every response includes `credits_used`: the credits this call cost.

Price: 1 credit per successful call. Docs: https://api.sh/docs/jcpenney-search

parameters.name: q
parameters.description: Search words. Optional when category or brand is given.

parameters.name: category
parameters.description: Category id from /jcpenney/v1/categories or categories[].id (e.g. cat100240063), or a jcpenney.com /g/ link with ?id=. Alone it browses the category; with q it narrows the search.

parameters.name: brand
parameters.description: Brand name in lower case as in facets (e.g. nike); several separated by | (any of them).

parameters.name: filters
parameters.description: More filters as name:value pairs separated by ; (several values of one name joined by |), using facets[].name and values, e.g. color:black;shoe_size:9|9 1/2;gender:women.

parameters.name: store
parameters.description: JCPenney store number (from /jcpenney/v1/stores): only products available for pickup there.

200.description: The data as JSON (or CSV / NDJSON with `output`).

get.description:
One JCPenney store by store number: name, mall, address, phone, coordinates, time zone, weekly and holiday hours, plus the full store record.

Every response includes `credits_used`: the credits this call cost.

Price: 1 credit per successful call. Docs: https://api.sh/docs/jcpenney-store

200.description: The data as JSON (or CSV / NDJSON with `output`).

get.description:
JCPenney stores near a US ZIP code, city or coordinates, nearest first: store number, store (mall) name, address, phone, coordinates, distance in miles, time zone, weekly hours and holiday hours. Pass `next_page` back as `page`; it is null on the last page.

Every response includes `credits_used`: the credits this call cost.

Price: 1 credit per successful call. Docs: https://api.sh/docs/jcpenney-stores

parameters.name: zip
parameters.description: 5-digit US ZIP code or a city such as Plano, TX (or use lat and lng).

200.description: The data as JSON (or CSV / NDJSON with `output`).

apiKey.name: x-api-key
apiKey.description: Create keys at https://app.api.sh/keys. Authorization: Bearer <key> also works.

raw.name: raw
raw.description: 0 leaves out the bulky `raw` source blocks (often 10-30x smaller).

fields.name: fields
fields.description: Comma-separated fields to return, e.g. `posts.id,posts.title`. Call metadata is always included.

fresh.name: fresh
fresh.description: 1 skips the 24-hour cache and fetches live.

output.name: output
output.description: csv or ndjson returns the response's records (its main list, or the object as one row) as CSV or NDJSON instead of JSON.

records.name: records
records.description: With output=csv|ndjson: the top-level list to turn into rows (e.g. `reviews`), or `.` for the whole object as one row.

status_url.description: On a 503 for a paused endpoint: the status page, which lists open incidents.

E400.description: A parameter is missing or invalid. Not charged (unless the call ran and the source rejected the value; credits_used says).

E401.description: Missing, invalid, revoked or expired API key. Not charged. See https://api.sh/docs/errors#401

E402.description: Not enough credits, a spend limit you set was reached (`spend_limit`), or the key's monthly credit cap was reached (`key_cap`). Not charged.

E404.description: Not found, or not public. A lookup that ran costs the endpoint's price (credits_used says); an unknown route is free.

E502.description: The source site failed this time; retry. Not charged.

E503.description: Endpoint paused or temporarily unavailable; may include retry-after, and status_url (https://api.sh/status) for a paused endpoint. Not charged.
